findings.title: queued default timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource instance gets the same stale process-start timestamp rather than the time the assignment was queued. The field is then serialized via to_dict and sent to the task, so the recorded time is wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: from_dict cannot round-trip the serialized queued timestamp
findings.body: to_dict uses asdict, which yields `queued` as a datetime object, but it is passed through Celery kwargs (JSON serialization) and back. When it arrives as an ISO string, cls(**input_dict) accepts it without type checking, so `queued` silently becomes a string; the from_dict contract and the field type disagree. Also unknown keys raise TypeError and are swallowed, returning None and silently disabling the loop-prevention check.

findings.title: should_sync signature change breaks other callers and overrides
findings.body: should_sync now takes a sync_source parameter, but sync_status_outbound and other call sites (e.g. where_should_sync in utils/sync.py line 48) still call should_sync(key) without it, and subclasses overriding should_sync with the old one-arg signature will raise TypeError when called with sync_source from sync_assignee_outbound. The change is not applied consistently across the integration base classes and implementations.

findings.title: Loop prevention only blocks outbound assignee sync, not the status sync path
findings.body: The sync_source check is added to should_sync generically, but sync_status_outbound also receives assignment_source and the fix is only applied to the assignee path. The issue describes cycles from inbound webhooks, and the status path is not guarded, so a status-triggered cycle through the same integration is not prevented. Also the check compares the source integration_id to the org integration's integration_id, which is only correct if the source is always an Integration row, not e.g. a plugin.

findings.title: assignment_source kwarg passed to implementations that may not accept it
findings.body: The task now calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...) unconditionally. Existing integration implementations of sync_assignee_outbound whose signature lacks **kwargs will fail with TypeError when called. The abstract method signature in IssueSyncIntegration was not updated to declare this parameter, so the contract is unclear.

findings.title: Assignment source is not forwarded on the create path or to subsequent re-assignments consistently
findings.body: The new assignment_source is only used when the outbound sync is triggered inside the affected branch; this is consistent with the other paths, but there is no test covering deassign with a matching source integration, so the deassign loop-prevention path is untested.

findings.title: No test covers the source-integration-matches path for deassign or the task-level parsing
findings.body: Tests cover only assign with a matching source. There is no test for deassign with an assignment_source from the same integration, nor for sync_assignee_outbound task receiving assignment_source_dict, so the new deserialization path in the task (including the invalid-dict fallback returning None) is untested at the integration boundary.
